messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for runtime v2.3.1 -> serving-pool 'hotwire'. Canary slice: 5% traffic. Release notes: kernel selection heuristics + microbatching change. Rolling out at 18:12 UTC.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: P50/P95/P99 latency spike detected on canary (serving-pool hotwire). Pager sent to #incidents and @michael (on-call).

sarah: seeing ~3x p99 on canary nodes vs baseline. Errors are 502s for a subset of requests. Happening within 2-3s after token generation starts.

raj: logs show frequent kernel fallback to scalar path on GPUs: "kernel_select: fallback=quant_scalar (reason=unsupported_wmma)". That would blow up latency for prompt shapes with long KV cache.

michael: confirming. I'm oncall, will take. Sarah — can you attach a sample trace?

sarah: pasted sample log: ```
[2026-03-17T18:14:02Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-hotwire seq=1024 kernel=quant_wmma -> fallback quant_scalar latency=1820ms
[2026-03-17T18:14:03Z] request_id=def456 model=redwood-hotwire seq=256 kernel=quant_wmma -> fallback quant_scalar latency=1340ms
```

tina: CS: we have 8 customers reporting slow responses in chat integrations. Three are high-touch enterprise customers (acct ids: 78-90). They're asking if this is related to today's deploy.

amos: quick triage — looks like the kernel selector is too aggressive on canary hardware profile (we changed microbatching heuristics). If we can flip the rollout back to the previous selector, should normalize. Suggest kill-switch for the new routing flag `ff.hotwire_kernel_v2`.

michael: agreed. Initiating emergency switchback. Steps: 1) pause canary 2) set ff.hotwire_kernel_v2=false 3) shift canary traffic to fallback pool.

raj: command to flip flag: `redwood feature toggle set ff.hotwire_kernel_v2 false --env=canary` (runs on control-plane). I'll run it and post status.

raj: (after) toggled `ff.hotwire_kernel_v2` -> false. Control plane shows 200 OK. Pushing config through to canary hosts now.

deploy-bot: Feature flag change propagated to 12 nodes in serving-pool 'hotwire' within 18s. Canary traffic paused by rollout manager. Traffic shift: canary -> baseline completed.

sarah: p99 back to baseline on the sampled hosts. Errors dropping to normal. Monitoring dashboards trending downwards.

tina: CC'ing affected customers with a short note: we experienced elevated latency during a canary rollout; mitigation applied (feature flag rollback) and we're monitoring. Will follow up with timeline.

ops-sre: preparing a postmortem template and collecting metrics (kernels chosen, batch sizes, seq lengths). Assigning action items: (1) tighten kernel selector safety checks (2) add canary gating for microbatch heuristic (3) alert tuning to detect kernel fallback rate.

incident-bot: Incident declared: hotwire-canary-latency-1834567890. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring for 1h. Postmortem owner: amos.

michael: handing off to amos for post-deploy follow-up & customer comms. If anything flares, ping me.

amos: taking it. I'll start the postmortem and schedule a follow-up with eng-runtime + cs in 30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
